Teaching view: movement through a vessel wall, followed by uptake and handling of an example target. Size and timing are illustrative.
Teaching view: contact and granule release at an example target surface. Size and timing are illustrative.
Teaching view: mediator release and a local vessel response. Size and timing are illustrative.
Teaching view: recruitment from blood into tissue. Some recruited monocytes become macrophages; this is one possible outcome.
Teaching view: a dendritic cell processes material and presents an antigen fragment to a T cell. Symbols do not represent molecular scale.
Teaching view: a plasma cell produces and releases antibodies. The pale Golgi region and protein-production structures are schematic.
Teaching view: a T cell responds to presented antigen and activation signals. Outcomes depend on the T-cell subtype.
Teaching view: one T-dependent B-cell response can lead to plasma cells or memory B cells. The receptor shapes are schematic.
Teaching view: an NK cell responds to an example altered target. Symbols and timing are illustrative.
Teaching view: a megakaryocyte extends cytoplasm near a vessel and releases platelet fragments. Scale and timing are illustrative.
Teaching view: activated platelets collect at a vessel injury and help form a plug. This is not a coagulation or treatment model.
Segmented nucleus
Mature neutrophils usually have several nuclear lobes joined by thin strands.
Fine granules
Fine cytoplasmic granules store proteins that help the cell respond to engulfed material.
Two nuclear lobes
The nucleus commonly has two lobes linked by a narrow bridge.
Eosin-binding granules
The large granules commonly stain orange to red with eosin.
Partly obscured nucleus
Coarse basophilic granules can make the underlying lobed nucleus hard to see.
Basophilic granules
The densely stained granules contain mediators such as histamine.
Indented nucleus
A monocyte often has an indented or kidney-shaped nucleus.
Cytoplasm and vacuoles
Monocytes have a broad rim of grey-blue cytoplasm; some contain small vacuoles.
Cell projection
The cell reshapes its membrane to move and surround material it will engulf.
Internal vesicle
Engulfed material is enclosed in a membrane-bound compartment before processing.
T-cell receptor
A T-cell receptor responds to particular antigens displayed by other cells. This is a receptor schematic, not an identification aid for a blood smear.
B-cell receptor
Membrane-bound immunoglobulin binds antigen on the B-cell surface. The drawing does not imply that B and T cells can be distinguished by shape.
Lymphocyte nucleus
The nucleus is often round and occupies much of a resting lymphocyte.
Cytotoxic granules
Natural killer cells store molecules used to induce death in selected target cells.
Eccentric nucleus
Dense chromatin often appears in clumps near the edge of the off-centre nucleus.
Golgi region
This comparatively pale region is near the machinery that processes secreted proteins.
Rough ER
Abundant rough endoplasmic reticulum supports antibody synthesis in a plasma cell.
Polyploid nucleus
DNA replication without cell division produces a large, lobulated nucleus in a maturing megakaryocyte.
Cytoplasmic extension
A maturing megakaryocyte can extend parts of its cytoplasm from which platelets form.
Anucleate disc
A resting platelet is a small cytoplasmic fragment without a cell nucleus.
Platelet granules
The central granules contain stored substances released during platelet activation.
Cell processes
Extended membrane processes are a schematic feature of dendritic cells and can vary with their state.
Nucleus
The nucleus contains the genetic material of the cell; this illustration does not identify a dendritic cell subtype.
